config.tacz.client.render.mesh_enable.de: Master switch of the built-in mesh loader. Off: mesh-pack guns draw without their poly parts (cube only), exactly as if the loader were absent. Models already loaded stay loaded - no restart needed either way.
config.tacz.client.render.mesh_poly_illu: Mesh Poly: Self-Lit Bones Keep Real Sky Light

Bones named *_illuminated are baked at max block AND max sky light so they stay visible in a dark cave (vanilla multiplies the two lightmap columns, so sky=0 would go black). Shader packs read that sky nibble as 'this surface can see the sun/moon', so those parts can never be shaded by a roof - the gun body inherits the sky brightness. With this on, and only while a shader pack is active, the sky component comes from the surrounding light while block stays 15. Off by default: it was written against an early reading of the shader report and the actual cause turned out to be something else, so enable it if you want self-lit parts to stop claiming they see the sky.
config.tacz.client.render.mesh_poly_mirr: Mesh Poly: Reverse Winding on Mirror

On by default for one round and then reverted: reversing it hides the outward faces on the normal (collector) route, because that one culls back faces - the gun renders inside-out and near-black. Off matches the original TML/Forge shading. The GPU route turns culling off, so there a winding change is subtle instead of fatal: enable it only to compare.
config.tacz.client.render.mesh_poly_inve: Extra global negation of the baked normals. If the highlights are still on the wrong side, try this and the winding option independently: with the winding left unreversed this reproduces the pre-R3 look, but it does not fix culling or gl_FrontFacing the way the winding option does. F3+T.
config.tacz.client.render.mesh_poly_pref: Use the per-vertex normals shipped in the mesh pack (smooth shading) instead of the flat normal computed from each face's cross product. Upstream has always forced flat shading, so barrels and handguards come out faceted; only packs that actually authored a normals array change. F3+T.
config.tacz.client.render.mesh_poly_in_p: Mesh Poly Parts In GUI Previews
Render poly parts in GUI / preview contexts (inventory, hotbar, gunsmith table, item frames viewed through a GUI). Off: those previews show the bedrock model only.
config.tacz.client.render.mesh_poly_in_s: Mesh Poly Parts In Shadow Pass
Only meaningful with a shader pack: also submit poly parts into the shadow pass so mesh guns cast shadows. Costs extra shadow-map geometry per gun, so it stays off by default.
config.tacz.client.render.mesh_log_stats: Log one line per loaded mesh model (bone count, vertex count, translucent/illuminated/magazine meshes). Verbose on large gun packs.
config.tacz.client.render.mesh_max_rende: Beyond this distance (blocks, measured on the pose matrix translation against the camera) poly parts are skipped in world contexts. 0 = unlimited.
config.tacz.client.render.mesh_gui_max_v: Per-model vertex budget for poly parts in GUI / FIXED / HEAD contexts; models above it fall back to cube-only or the pack-provided LOD model. 0 = unlimited.
config.tacz.client.render.mesh_world_max: Per-model vertex budget for third-person, dropped items and item frames; models above it fall back to cube-only or the pack-provided LOD model. 0 = unlimited. Not consulted while the GPU world path is live for that gun - that path uploads O(bones) matrices per frame and has no per-vertex CPU cost to protect.
config.tacz.client.render.mesh_max_model: Log a warning while loading a model with more vertices than this. Purely informational - it does not change rendering. 0 = never warn.
config.tacz.client.render.mesh_gpu_bakin: Bake first-person poly_mesh gun models into resident GPU buffers, uploading only bone matrices each frame. Massively reduces CPU cost for high-poly (100k+ vertex) mesh guns. GUI and preview contexts always keep the collector path; world contexts are covered by the in-world option below. Falls back to the CPU path by itself if the GPU pass fails - the guard only flips an in-memory flag, it never writes this config file.
config.tacz.client.render.mesh_gpu_under: Mesh GPU: Resident VBO Under Shaders

Keeps GPU-baked mesh guns on the resident-VBO path when a shader pack is active: the pass is opened inside Iris' own hand flush, so it lands in the gbuffer and is lit by the pack's hand program instead of being re-transformed on the CPU every frame. Needs an audited Iris 1.10.x; if the flush hook is not live the submissions are refused and the gun falls back to the normal collector path. Off by default again: R3 turned it on after an in-game pass, but mesh gun geometry was then seen to inherit the sun/moon brightness wherever it covered them, and only switching this and the world option off removed it - the resident-VBO path is not lighting-equivalent under a shader pack yet. Enable it to help compare.
config.tacz.client.render.mesh_gpu_world: Mesh GPU: In-World Contexts (Third-Person / Drops / Frames)

Keeps mesh guns held by other players, dropped items, item frames and display statues on the resident-VBO path: each gun uploads O(bones) matrices per frame instead of every vertex being transformed on the CPU. GUI, screen-embedded previews, the in-scope pass and shadow passes are refused at submit time and keep the collector path; per-light-level VBOs are cached (Mesh GPU: World Light Levels Cached). Falls back to the collector path automatically if the world flush hook stops firing, and the reason is logged once per distinct cause.

Also keeps in-world mesh guns on the resident-VBO path when a shader pack is active, lit through the pack's entity program (the custom pipeline is registered with IrisApi.assignPipeline(IrisProgram.ENTITIES), constant audited against the Iris 1.10.7 jar). Same audited-flush-hook requirement as the hand path, same automatic fallback. Off by default for the same reason as the hand option - the artefact showed in third person and on display stands too, so the world path is affected in exactly the same way.
config.tacz.client.render.mesh_gpu_light: Mesh GPU: World Light Levels Cached

How many quantized light levels of baked world VBOs to keep per gun model (LRU, 1-16). Upstream TML caches 8 unquantized levels; this port quantizes light first (4 steps each for block and sky light), so 4 covers nearly every scene. Each cached level costs GPU memory proportional to the model's vertex count. First-person baking is unaffected - it keeps a single level.
config.tacz.client.render.mesh_world_ful: Within this distance (blocks), high-poly mesh guns in the world (third-person, dropped items, item frames, display statues) always render in full detail, ignoring the vertex budget. Without this, dense guns lacking a pack-provided LOD model would vanish to cube-only right in front of you. Beyond this distance the vertex budget applies as usual. 0 = no exemption.
